title: Injuries as a result of cyclical adaptation failure
summary: He frames injuries as a failure to adapt to a cycle of stress and recovery, and puts the responsibility on the lifter. The cycle has three arrows: movements suited to your morphology, enough recovery, and the right volume and intensity.
claims: Injuries do not just happen; freak injuries are rare
Responsibility for injury is on you; if you know your body and something happens, it was your fault
Injuries are a failure to adapt to a cycle of stress
Joint stress in lifting is unavoidable and normal; joints are meant to be used and would atrophy or calcify without movement
For naturals, tendon injuries caused by muscle strength outpacing tendon strength are very unlikely unless you do very short range of motion lifts
Injury comes from not letting stress wash away through recovery, or from movements your body does not tolerate

Your joints should not adapt to you; you adapt to your body: some people cannot pull conventional without excess lumbar shear or squat with certain foot positions without knee stress, and leverages cannot be changed
You are the pilot of your body; blaming a structurally weak body is a cop-out
Three arrows of the cycle: movements suited to your morphology, enough recovery time for joints and protein synthesis, and matching volume and intensity
The cycle can grow over time: as muscles grow and a male ages, the hormonal environment keeps up so volume and intensity can increase without lowering frequency
Respect for your body and movements must be permanent, but once figured out it is easy to maintain
